title: Telemetry IaC: 'Healthyard' VPC observability module with canary upgrades and log-forwarding orchestration
creator: Riley Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module ("Healthyard") for deploying the full VPC observability stack in private deployments. The module will provision and manage: Prometheus (operator/values via Helm), Grafana with curated dashboards and provisioning, OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) with configurable pipelines (OTLP/receivers/exporters), and a log-shipping component (Vector/Fluent Bit) to S3/Syslog/Splunk. It must support safe upgrades (canary subsets, pre/post health gates), lifecycle hooks (drain, KV cache warm-up, dashboards sync), and integration points for Dedicated/Hosted fallback policies. The goal is a single module teams can consume in customer VPCs with opinionated defaults, but flexible overrides for enterprise integrations (KMS, Splunk credentials, retention).
tasks: Design Terraform module interface: variables for canary percentage, helm chart overrides, storage backends, nodeSelector/taints
Implement Helm provider + Kubernetes provider wiring and remote state outputs
Add canary upgrade orchestration: create separate canary release namespace and traffic mirroring rules
Implement health gates: readiness checks, custom probe endpoint on collector and prom-operator webhook integration
Add lifecycle hooks: pre-upgrade drain script, post-upgrade smoke tests (query/OTLP round-trip), KV cache warm-up cron
Wire secrets handling: integrate with KMS/HSM patterns and optional external secret manager
Add automated dashboard provisioning (Grafana) and migration path for user dashboards
Add log-shipping templates and S3/HTTP/Splunk outputs with rotation/retention settings
Write acceptance tests using kind/eksctl and local helm charts; add CI job in infra pipeline
Document module usage and migration checklist for on-prem customers
acceptance_criteria: Module can deploy Prometheus + Grafana + OTel + Vector to a private VPC via Terraform with a single call
Module supports toggling canary mode; canary deploys receive mirrored traffic and pass health gates before full rollout
Automated pre/post upgrade hooks execute and will roll back on health-gate failures
Grafana dashboards are provisioned and show metrics from the deployed Prometheus instance
OTel collector accepts OTLP and forwards to configured backends (prometheus remote_write, logging sinks) with >=95% success rate in smoke tests
Log shipping to S3 preserves ordering for a 24h test window and adheres to retention TTL
risks: Helm provider drift: differing Helm chart versions across customer clusters may require multiple override code paths
Stateful component upgrades (Prometheus) may cause data loss if snapshots/retention not managed during upgrades
Resource constraints in small customer VPCs could cause pods to be OOM/killed during canary testing
Secrets and KMS integration vary by customer — misconfiguration could lead to data exfil risk if not validated
S3/Splunk throughput limits could create backpressure on Vector causing logs to buffer and increase memory usage
qa_plan: Create CI job that runs terraform plan/apply against a disposable EKS cluster and asserts all resources become Ready
Run canary upgrade scenario: deploy v1, inject synthetic metrics and logs, deploy v2 canary, validate mirrored traffic and health gates, promote to v2 full rollout
Failure injection tests: simulate Prometheus scrape failure and ensure automated rollback triggers
Load test log-shipping with 10k events/min and observe memory/latency characteristics
Security validate secret rotation and KMS envelope decryption on deployed pods
